doc.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997

title: Throat injury, ten years off the trumpet and studying with Penzarella
summary: Self-taught habits tore a throat muscle; he quit for ten years, had an operation at 19, and later restarted with teacher Vince Penzarella.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: That coupled with the fact that I was pretty much self-taught. I had some lessons but as far as just basic technique, I had a few bad habits that really caught up with me with a vengeance. To make a long story short, I ended up developing this problem in my throat which was kind of like a hernia. There’s a tear in the muscle in my throat which got worse and worse and worse kind of through my first couple of years of college to the point that I just decided screw this.
Yes. So I ended up quitting for ten years.
Yeah. I didn’t touch the horn.

Well when I was 19 I had an operation on it, which at the time, because I really didn’t know what was causing the problem, and I was kind of perpetuating the same bad habits, that after it healed and everything and I started playing, it started doing the same thing. So I didn’t think it was a success. But I think it had pretty much, it had taken care of the problems. So ten years later when I started playing again, which was almost totally by accident, I immediately decided well if I’m going to do this I want to start with a teacher, an excellent classical player, started studying with this man Vince Penzarella who plays in the Philharmonic and is great. He taught Jon Faddis and Wynton Marsalis and you know, I just can’t say enough about the guy. He’s great. And he also, he had been in a car accident and really messed up his face and so he had to start — he had been a professional and he had to start again. And so he’d been through a similar thing and he really had to analyze how you do it. So that was just perfect to have hooked up with him at the time I did and just start over with a clean slate. And he really made me understand just the basic dynamics of playing the trumpet, which are fairly simple but whether you get them intuitively or learn them, I mean it’s like the laws of physics and biology. I mean you have to work in harmony with them. If you don’t it’s going to be trouble. So you learn those thing, you absorb that, and then you can go on.
